root_cause.text: In the 9p mount-option handling path, v9fs_apply_options() incorrectly ORed user-selected access-mode bits into v9ses->flags instead of replacing the existing V9FS_ACCESS_MASK set by v9fs_session_init(), leaving an invalid combined access mode that exact-value checks in v9fs_fid_lookup() did not recognize.
root_cause.evidence: The commit/CVE states that after commit 1f3e4142c0eb, v9fs_apply_options() used "|=" on flags already initialized with V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT, so mounting with "access=user" set both bits; the patch fixes this by clearing V9FS_ACCESS_MASK first (`if (ctx->session_opts.flags & V9FS_ACCESS_MASK) v9ses->flags &= ~V9FS_ACCESS_MASK;`) before ORing in the new flags.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear existing access-mode bits before applying parsed 9p session access flags so option-selected access settings override defaults correctly.
intent_record.what: In v9fs_apply_options(), a new conditional was added before OR-ing session option flags into v9ses->flags: if ctx->session_opts.flags contains any bits in V9FS_ACCESS_MASK, the code now clears those bits from v9ses->flags using &= ~V9FS_ACCESS_MASK. A comment was also added explaining that default access flags must be cleared when session options change them.
intent_record.how: Previously, access-mode bits already set in v9ses->flags could remain combined with newly parsed access flags because the code only used |=, potentially producing an incorrect mixed access setting. The new logic removes existing access bits first when new access flags are present, so the runtime session uses the requested access mode cleanly instead of inheriting conflicting default bits.

grouping_result.intent: Clear existing access-mode bits before applying parsed 9p session access flags so option-selected access settings override defaults correctly.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by clearing the existing V9FS_ACCESS_MASK before applying parsed access flags, ensuring user-selected access mode replaces the default instead of being ORed into it.

candidates.rationale: This ORs parsed mount-option flags into the existing session flags instead of replacing the preexisting V9FS_ACCESS_MASK bits set during session initialization, allowing incompatible access-mode bits to remain combined and later fail exact-value checks.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement merges parsed mount-option flags into the existing session flags with |=, preserving previously initialized V9FS_ACCESS_MASK bits instead of replacing them. As a result, incompatible access-mode bits can remain combined, producing an invalid access mode that later exact-value checks do not recognize.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows both the parsing of the access option and the later application of parsed flags into the live session. In `v9fs_parse_param()`, the access option correctly clears the access mask in the temporary parsed options: `session_opts->flags &= ~V9FS_ACCESS_MASK;` and then sets one of `V9FS_ACCESS_USER`, `V9FS_ACCESS_ANY`, `V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT`, or `V9FS_ACCESS_SINGLE`. However, in `v9fs_apply_options()` the parsed flags are merged into the real session with `v9ses->flags |= ctx->session_opts.flags;`. The comment even states: `v9fs_apply_options below will |= the additional flags from parsed options.` In `v9fs_session_init()`, `v9ses->flags` is initialized first with `v9ses->flags = V9FS_ACCESS_USER;`. Therefore, if the user selected a different access mode such as `any` or `client`, `v9fs_apply_options()` ORs that new mode on top of the existing default access mode instead of replacing the existing `V9FS_ACCESS_MASK`, exactly matching the root cause. There is no corresponding fix in `v9fs_apply_options()` to clear `V9FS_ACCESS_MASK` on `v9ses->flags` before applying the parsed access mode, so the function still contains the vulnerable construct and does not yet contain the fix.

This snippet is the session initialization function, not v9fs_apply_options(), and the only option-related call shown is `rc = v9fs_parse_options(v9ses, data);` at line 343. The function does show initialization of `v9ses->flags` (`v9ses->flags = V9FS_ACCESS_USER;` at line 334, later possibly set to `V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT` at lines 336-338) and it does contain later exact-value checks/mask replacement logic such as `((v9ses->flags & V9FS_ACCESS_MASK) == V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT)` and explicit clearing with `v9ses->flags &= ~V9FS_ACCESS_MASK;` at lines 357-358 and 365-366. However, the actual vulnerable construct described—ORing user-selected access bits during option application—is not visible here.
